messages.subject: std::log(x) vs. ::log(x) vs. log(x)?
parts:
I'm confused about which namespaces log (and exp) are
defined in. (The context is that I'm cleaning
out global "using ..." statements and making them
local and we have a "using std::log; using std::exp;"
in the math namespace.

For a start, I'm confused as to why this program
compiles and links and runs:

-------------------
#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>

int main(int argc, const char* argv[]) {
std::cout << "hello exp(2)=" << exp(2) << std::endl;
std::cout << "hello log(3)=" << log(3) << std::endl;
}
------------------

I don't know how to figure out which version of exp() and
log() these unqualified calls make.

The program still works if I add that I want
log() and exp() from the global namespace:

-------------------
#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>

int main(int argc, const char* argv[]) {
std::cout << "hello exp(2)=" << ::exp(2) << std::endl;
std::cout << "hello log(3)=" << ::log(3) << std::endl;
}
------------------

But it doesn't work if I remove the "#include <cmath>".

From everything I read, including <cmath> (instead of <math>)
will include the C++ versions of exp() and log() which
are in namespace std. How are they getting into the global
namespace? Is it the same function?

- Bob
